misconceptions.description: Assuming static friction always equals μsN
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes Fs = μsN before checking impending motion
misconceptions.feedback: Static friction is variable and adjusts up to its maximum value. Fs = μsN is only valid at impending motion.

misconceptions.description: Choosing friction direction based only on the applied force instead of impending relative motion
misconceptions.trigger: learner points friction in the wrong direction on a surface or incline
misconceptions.feedback: Friction opposes the actual or impending relative motion at the contact surface, not just whichever applied force looks largest.

misconceptions.description: Assuming the normal force always equals the full weight
misconceptions.trigger: learner sets N = mg on an incline without resolving components
misconceptions.feedback: The normal force equals the component of weight perpendicular to the surface only when the geometry supports that relation.
